1564.subject: Physics
1564.text: A person used force $(F)$, shown in figure to move a load with constant velocity on surface. Identify the correct surface profile.
1564.sol:
First a force is used to move the body when it has to be more than the static friction. Then the body starts moving and is getting accelerated. Then
suddenly the force is decreased to match the kinetic friction. The body then moves with a constant velocity. Force $>\mu_s \cdot N$. Constant acceleration, velocity increases proportionately with time. Then suddenly force applied is just equal to $\mu_K N$. It is just sufficient to cancel friction. Whatever be the earlier maximum velocity attained will be continued.

5030.sol: Superoxides are the species having an $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}$ bond and $\mathrm{O}$ in an oxidation state of $-\frac{1}{2}$ (superoxide ion is $\mathrm{O}_2^{-}$). Usually these are formed by active metals such as $\mathrm{KO}_2, \mathrm{RbO}_2$ and $\mathrm{CsO}_2$. For the salts of larger anions (like $\mathrm{O}_2^{-}$), lattice energy increases in a group. 7957.text: If ${a}_{1}, {a}_{2}, . . . , {a}_{9}$ are in $G . P . ,$ then $\left|\begin{cases}log{a}_{1} & log{a}_{2} & log{a}_{3} \\ log{a}_{4} & log{a}_{5} & log{a}_{6} \\ log{a}_{7} & log{a}_{8} & log{a}_{9}\end{cases}\right|$ is equal to
7957.sol:
Given& ${a}_{1}, {a}_{2}, {a}_{3}, . . . , {a}_{9}$ are in& $G . P . ,$ hence, by the definition of $G . P . ,$ we have& $\dfrac{a2}{a1} = \dfrac{a3}{a2} = \dfrac{a4}{a3} = . . . \dfrac{a9}{a8} = r,$ where& $r$ is the common ratio of the& $G . P .$

Now, let $△ = \left|\begin{cases}log{a}_{1} & log{a}_{2} & log{a}_{3} \\ log{a}_{4} & log{a}_{5} & log{a}_{6} \\ log{a}_{7} & log{a}_{8} & log{a}_{9}\end{cases}\right|$

Applying ${C}_{2} \to {C}_{2} - {C}_{1}, {C}_{3} \to {C}_{3} - {C}_{2},$ we get

$△ = \left|\begin{cases}log{a}_{1} & log{a}_{2} - log{a}_{1} & log{a}_{3} - log{a}_{2} \\ log{a}_{4} & log{a}_{5} - log{a}_{4} & log{a}_{6} - log{a}_{5} \\ log{a}_{7} & log{a}_{8} - log{a}_{7} & log{a}_{9} - log{a}_{8}\end{cases}\right|$

Using $logm - logn = log\left(\dfrac{m}{n}\right),$ we get

$⇒ △ = \left|\begin{cases}log{a}_{1} & log\left(\dfrac{a2}{a1}\right) & log\left(\dfrac{a3}{a2}\right) \\ log{a}_{4} & log\left(\dfrac{a5}{a4}\right) & log\left(\dfrac{a6}{a5}\right) \\ log{a}_{7} & log\left(\dfrac{a8}{a7}\right) & log\left(\dfrac{a9}{a8}\right)\end{cases}\right|$

Using the relation defined above, we get

$⇒ △ = \left|\begin{cases}log{a}_{1} & log\left(r\right) & log\left(r\right) \\ log{a}_{4} & log\left(r\right) & log\left(r\right) \\ log{a}_{7} & log\left(r\right) & log\left(r\right)\end{cases}\right|$

Thus, the determinant has& ${C}_{2} = {C}_{3},$ and we know that if two rows/columns of a determinant are same then its value is zero.

So,& $△ = \left|\begin{cases}log{a}_{1} & log{a}_{2} & log{a}_{3} \\ log{a}_{4} & log{a}_{5} & log{a}_{6} \\ log{a}_{7} & log{a}_{8} & log{a}_{9}\end{cases}\right| = 0 .$

\Rightarrow \quad y & =\frac{10^{2 x}-1}{10^{2 x}+1}\\
\Rightarrow \quad 10^{2 x} y+y & =10^{2 x}-1 \\
\Rightarrow \quad 10^{2 x}(y-1) & =-(y+1) \\
\Rightarrow \quad & 10^{2 x} & =\frac{y+1}{1-y}\\
\Rightarrow \quad & 2 x & =\log _{10}\frac{y+1}{1-y}\\
\Rightarrow \quad x & =\frac{1}{2} \log _{10} \left(\frac{1+y}{1-y}\right) \\
\therefore \quad & f^{-1}(x) & =\frac{1}{2} \log _{10}\left(\frac{1+x}{1-x}\right)
\end{array}$

9901.text: The solution of the linear system of equations $\left[\begin{cases}2 & 2 & 3 \\ 7 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 6 & 5\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ll}x \\ y \\ z\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}3y + 11 \\ 6z - 1 \\ 5y + 11\end{array}\right] + \left[\begin{array}{ll}x \\ x \\ 4z\end{array}\right] + \left[\begin{array}{ll}z \\ 3x \\ 4y\end{array}\right]$ is
9901.sol:
It is given that

$\left[\begin{cases}2 & 2 & 3 \\ 7 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 6 & 5\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ll}x \\ y \\ z\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}3y + 11 \\ 6z - 1 \\ 5y + 11\end{array}\right] + \left[\begin{array}{ll}x \\ x \\ 4z\end{array}\right] + \left[\begin{array}{ll}z \\ 3x \\ 4y\end{array}\right]$

Solve the above matrix

$\left[\begin{array}{ll}2x + 2y + 3z \\ 7x + y + z \\ 6y + 5z\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}3y + x + z + 11 \\ 3x + x + 6z - 1 \\ 5y + 4y + 4z + 11\end{array}\right]$

$\left[\begin{array}{ll}2x + 2y + 3z \\ 7x + y + z \\ 6y + 5z\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}x + 3y + z + 11 \\ 4x + 6z - 1 \\ 9y + 4z + 11\end{array}\right]$

On comparing
$x - y + 2z = 11$

$⇒ 3x + y - 5z = - 1$

$⇒ - 3y + z = 11$

From the above three equations

$x = 4, y = - 3, z = 2$

The area of the triangle formed is given by

$\begin{aligned}$& =$\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{k}{3} \times \frac{k}{4} \Rightarrow$6=$\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{k^2}{12}$\\
& \Rightarrow k²=12 $\times$12 \Rightarrow k= $\pm$12
\end{aligned}

Thus,$ the equation of line becomes4 x+3 y= \pm 12 or 4 x+3 y \pm 12=0$
For minimum distance from point $(1,1)$, we will take negative sign.
So, the equation of line is $4 x+3 y-12=0$
The required distance $=\left|\frac{4 \times 1+3 \times 1-12}{\sqrt{4^2+3^2}}\right|$
=$\left|\frac{4+3-12}{5}\right|$=$\frac{5}{5} \Rightarrow=$1

13642.text: The ionization potential of hydrogen atom is $13. 6V$. How much energy need to be supplied to ionize the hydrogen atom in the first excited state.
13642.sol:
Ionization energy& is the minimum amount of energy required to remove the most loosely bound electron of an isolated neutral gaseous atom or molecule.

Energy of an orbit is inversely proportional to the square of principal quantum number, $E ∝ \dfrac{1}{n2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{E2}{E1} = \dfrac{{n}_{1}2}{{n}_{2}2}$

$⇒ {E}_{2} = \dfrac{E1}{22}$

$⇒ {E}_{2} = \dfrac{13. 6}{4}$

$⇒ {E}_{2} = 3. 4eV$

When block of mass~$1 . 5kg$~hits the ground, at that time block of mass& $0 . 5kg$~will be at a height of& $80$ cm~from the ground. After this point string become slack and block& $B$~will move with deceleration& $g = 10ms^{- 2} .$

Using third~equation of motion, speed of block $B,$~When& block& $A$~Reaches the ground-

$v^{2} = 0 + 2\left(\dfrac{g}{2}\right)\left(\dfrac{80}{100}\right) = 8$

$⇒ v = \sqrt{8}ms^{- 1}$

Again using third~equation& of motion, suppose block& $B$~will further move upto a height of& $hm .$

$0 = v^{2} + 2\left(- 10\right)h$

$⇒ h = \dfrac{v2}{20} = 0 . 4m = 40cm$

hence, total height of block~$B$~from the ground

$= 80 + 40 = 120cm$

19916.subject: Chemistry
19916.text: For the reaction $2 \mathrm{ N}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{5} \longrightarrow 4 \mathrm{NO}_{2}+\mathrm{O}_{2}$, rate constant $k$ is $4.48 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{ s}^{-1}$ and the initial pressure is $600 \mathrm{ atm}$. After $10 \mathrm{ min}$, determine the final pressure of $\mathrm{N}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{5}$.
19916.sol:
The reaction is $2 \mathrm{N}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{5} \rightarrow 4 \mathrm{NO}_{2} + \mathrm{O}_{2}$. Since the rate constant $k$ has units of $\mathrms^{-1}$, the reaction is a first-order reaction.

The integrated rate law for a first-order reaction is given by $P_{t} = P_{0} e^{-kt}$, where $P_{t}$ is the pressure of the reactant at time $t$, $P_{0}$ is the initial pressure, $k$ is the rate constant, and $t$ is the time.

Given values are $P_{0} = 600 \mathrm{ atm}$, $k = 4.48 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{ s}^{-1}$, and $t = 10 \mathrm{ min} = 600 \mathrm{ s}$.

Substituting these values into the equation:

$P_{t} = 600 \times e^{-(4.48 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{ s}^{-1}) \times (600 \mathrm{ s})}$

$P_{t} = 600 \times e^{-0.02688}$

Using the approximation $e^{-x} \approx 1 - x$ for small $x$:

$P_{t} \approx 600 \times (1 - 0.02688)$

$P_{t} \approx 600 \times 0.97312$

$P_{t} \approx 583.87 \mathrm{ atm}$.

Alternatively, using the exact value $e^{-0.02688} \approx 0.97347$:

$P_{t} = 600 \times 0.97347 = 584.08 \mathrm{ atm}$.

Answer: 584 atm

20156.text:
$Arrange the following redox couples in the increasing order of their reducing strength:
\begin{array}{ll}
{[\mathrm{A}]=\mathrm{Cu} / \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}} & \mathrm{E}^0=-0.34 \mathrm{ V} \\

The reducing strength of a species is determined by its standard oxidation potential. A higher standard oxidation potential (E^{0}_{ox}$) indicates a stronger reducing agent. The given values are standard oxidation potentials (E^{0}_{ox}$) for the couples $M/M^{n+}$.

B: $Ag/Ag^{+}$, $E^{0}_{ox} = -0.8$ V

Comparing the values:
$-0.8 < -0.34 < +0.74 < +2.87$

This corresponds to the order:
B < A < D < C

Thus, the increasing order of reducing strength is B < A < D < C.

21004.subject: Mathematics
21004.text: The area of the region enclosed by the lines $2 x+y=10, y=1, y=5$ and the y -axis is
21004.sol:
The region is bounded by the lines $2x + y = 10$, $y = 1$, $y = 5$, and the y-axis ($x = 0$).

Expressing $x$ in terms of $y$ from the equation $2x + y = 10$, we get $x = \dfrac{10 - y}{2} = 5 - 0.5y$.

The area $A$ of the region is given by the integral of $x$ with respect to $y$ from $y = 1$ to $y = 5$:

$A = \int_{1}^{5} (5 - 0.5y) dy$

$A = [5y - 0.25y^2]_{1}^{5}$

$A = (5(5) - 0.25(5)^2) - (5(1) - 0.25(1)^2)$

$A = (25 - 6.25) - (5 - 0.25)$

$A = 18.75 - 4.75 = 14$.

Alternatively, the region is a trapezoid with parallel sides along the lines $y=1$ and $y=5$. At $y=1$, $x = \dfrac{10-1}{2} = 4.5$. At $y=5$, $x = \dfrac{10-5}{2} = 2.5$. The height of the trapezoid is $5 - 1 = 4$. The area is $\dfrac{1}{2} \times (4.5 + 2.5) \times 4 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 7 \times 4 = 14$.

Answer: 14 sq units

22240.sol:
Let $\theta = 20^{{}^{\circ}}$. The expression is $E = \dfrac{\sin^{2}\theta + \cos^{4}\theta}{\sin^{4}\theta + \cos^{2}\theta}$.

Using the identity $\sin^{2}\theta = 1 - \cos^{2}\theta$, we substitute into the numerator:

Numerator $= (1 - \cos^{2}\theta) + \cos^{4}\theta = 1 - \cos^{2}\theta + \cos^{4}\theta$.

Using the identity $\cos^{2}\theta = 1 - \sin^{2}\theta$, we substitute into the denominator:

Denominator $= \sin^{4}\theta + (1 - \sin^{2}\theta) = 1 - \sin^{2}\theta + \sin^{4}\theta$.

Since $\cos^{2}\theta = 1 - \sin^{2}\theta$, the numerator becomes $1 - (1 - \sin^{2}\theta) + (1 - \sin^{2}\theta)^{2} = 1 - 1 + \sin^{2}\theta + 1 - 2\sin^{2}\theta + \sin^{4}\theta = 1 - \sin^{2}\theta + \sin^{4}\theta$.

Thus, the numerator is equal to the denominator, so $E = 1$.

Answer: $1$

22436.subject: Physics
22436.text: In a hydrogen atom, if electron is replaced by a particle which is 40 times heavier but has the same charge, then, the ratio of the radius of the first excited state of a normal hydrogen atom to the ground state of the above atom is
22436.sol:
The radius of the $n$-th orbit of a hydrogen-like atom is given by $r_n = \dfrac{n^2 a_0}{Z} \times \dfrac{m_e}{m}$, where $m$ is the mass of the particle and $a_0$ is the Bohr radius of the hydrogen atom ($a_0 = \dfrac{h^2}{4\pi^2 m_e e^2}$).

For a normal hydrogen atom, $m = m_e$, $Z = 1$, and the first excited state corresponds to $n = 2$. Thus, $r_{H} = \dfrac{2^2 a_0}{1} = 4 a_0$.

For the new atom, the particle mass is $m' = 40 m_e$, $Z = 1$, and the ground state corresponds to $n = 1$. Thus, $r' = \dfrac{1^2}{1} \times \dfrac{m_e}{40 m_e} a_0 = \dfrac{a_0}{40}$.

The ratio of the radius of the first excited state of the normal hydrogen atom to the ground state of the new atom is $\dfrac{r_H}{r'} = \dfrac{4 a_0}{a_0 / 40} = 4 \times 40 = 160$.

Therefore, the ratio is $160 : 1$.

Answer: 160 : 1

23114.subject: Physics
23114.text: The square of resultant of two equal electric field vectors is three times their product. Angle between them is
23114.sol:
Let the two equal electric field vectors be $\vec{E_1}$ and $\vec{E_2}$ such that $|\vec{E_1}| = |\vec{E_2}| = E$.

The resultant vector $\vec{R} = \vec{E_1} + \vec{E_2}$ has a magnitude given by $R^2 = E^2 + E^2 + 2E^2 \cos \theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between the two vectors.

$R^2 = 2E^2(1 + \cos \theta) = 2E^2(2 \cos^2 \dfrac{\theta}{2}) = 4E^2 \cos^2 \dfrac{\theta}{2}$.

The problem states that the square of the resultant is three times the product of the magnitudes of the two vectors, which is $3(E \times E) = 3E^2$.

Equating the two expressions for $R^2$:

$4E^2 \cos^2 \dfrac{\theta}{2} = 3E^2$

$\cos^2 \dfrac{\theta}{2} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$\cos \dfrac{\theta}{2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$\dfrac{\theta}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$

Resonance occurs when the driving frequency of an external periodic force matches the natural frequency of the system.

Under this condition, the energy transfer from the driving force to the oscillator is maximized, leading to a significant increase in the amplitude of oscillation.

The frequency and time period of the oscillation are determined by the system's natural properties and do not necessarily become large; rather, the system oscillates at its natural frequency with a greatly increased amplitude.

Answer: the amplitude of oscillation becomes large

23458.subject: Physics
23458.text: In the circuit given, the reverse breakdown voltage of the Zener diode is 4.8 V. The current through the Zener and the power dissipation in Zener is:
23458.sol:
Given:
Input voltage, $V = 12\ \text{V}$
Zener voltage, $V_z = 4.8\ \text{V}$
Series resistance, $R_s = 250\ \Omega$
Load resistance, $R_L = 750\ \Omega$

First, we check if the Zener diode is in the breakdown region. The voltage across the load without the Zener diode is:
$V' = \dfrac{R_L}{R_s + R_L} \times V = \dfrac{750}{250 + 750} \times 12 = 9\ \text{V}$

Since $V' > V_z$, the Zener diode is in breakdown and the voltage across the load is clamped at $V_z = 4.8\ \text{V}$.

The current through the series resistor $R_s$ is:
$I = \dfrac{V - V_z}{R_s} = \dfrac{12 - 4.8}{250} = \dfrac{7.2}{250} = 0.0288\ \text{A} = 28.8\ \text{mA}$

The current through the load resistor $R_L$ is:
$I_r = \dfrac{V_z}{R_L} = \dfrac{4.8}{750} = 0.0064\ \text{A} = 6.4\ \text{mA}$

The current through the Zener diode is:
$I_z = I - I_r = 28.8\ \text{mA} - 6.4\ \text{mA} = 22.4\ \text{mA}$

The power dissipated in the Zener diode is:
$P_z = V_z \times I_z = 4.8\ \text{V} \times 22.4\ \text{mA} = 107.52\ \text{mW}$

Answer: $22.4\ \text{mA};\ 107.52\ \text{mW}$

25371.subject: Mathematics
25371.text:
Consider the function $f : \left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) \rightarrow (-\infty, \infty)$ defined by

$f(x) = (|x| + |x - 1|) \sin x + [x \sin x]$,

where $[x \sin x]$ is the greatest integer less than or equal to $x \sin x$.

Let $\alpha$ be the total number of points in the interval $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ at which $f$ is NOT continuous, and let $\beta$ be the total number of points in the interval $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ at which $f$ is NOT differentiable.

Then the value of $\alpha + \beta$ is ___________.
25371.sol:
Let $f(x) = g(x) + h(x)$, where $g(x) = (|x| + |x - 1|) \sin x$ and $h(x) = [x \sin x]$.

First, we analyze $h(x) = [x \sin x]$ on the interval $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$.
The function $y = x \sin x$ is an even function. For $x \in \left[0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, $x \sin x$ is strictly increasing.
At $x = 0$, $x \sin x = 0$.
As $x \to \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, $x \sin x \to \dfrac{\pi}{2} \approx 1.57$.
Thus, $x \sin x \in [0, 1.57)$ for $x \in \left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$.
The value of $[x \sin x]$ will be $0$ when $0 \le x \sin x < 1$, and $1$ when $1 \le x \sin x < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
Let $x_1 \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ be the unique point where $x_1 \sin x_1 = 1$. By symmetry, $-x_1$ is the unique point in $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, 0\right)$ where $(-x_1) \sin(-x_1) = 1$.
Therefore, $h(x)$ has jump discontinuities at exactly two points: $x = x_1$ and $x = -x_1$.
At $x = 0$, $x \sin x = 0$ and is non-negative in its neighborhood, so $[x \sin x] = 0$ around $x = 0$, making $h(x)$ continuous and differentiable at $x = 0$.

Next, we analyze $g(x) = (|x| + |x - 1|) \sin x$.
The absolute value functions have critical points at $x = 0$ and $x = 1$.
For $x$ in a small neighborhood of $0$ (specifically $x \in (-1, 1)$):
If $x \in [0, 1)$, $g(x) = (x - (x - 1)) \sin x = \sin x \Rightarrow g'(0^+) = \cos 0 = 1$.
If $x \in (-1, 0)$, $g(x) = (-x - (x - 1)) \sin x = (1 - 2x) \sin x \Rightarrow g'(0^-) = -2 \sin 0 + 1 \cdot \cos 0 = 1$.
Since $g'(0^+) = g'(0^-)$, $g(x)$ is differentiable at $x = 0$.

For $x$ in a small neighborhood of $1$:
If $x \in (0, 1]$, $g(x) = \sin x \Rightarrow g'(1^-) = \cos 1$.
If $x \in \left(1, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, $g(x) = (x + (x - 1)) \sin x = (2x - 1) \sin x \Rightarrow g'(1^+) = 2 \sin 1 + 1 \cdot \cos 1$.
Since $g'(1^-) \neq g'(1^+)$, $g(x)$ is not differentiable at $x = 1$.

Now, combining the results for $f(x) = g(x) + h(x)$:
1. Discontinuities: $g(x)$ is continuous everywhere. $h(x)$ is discontinuous at $x_1$ and $-x_1$. Thus, $f(x)$ is discontinuous at $2$ points. $\Rightarrow \alpha = 2$.
2. Non-differentiability: $f(x)$ is not differentiable where it is discontinuous ($x_1$ and $-x_1$). Additionally, at $x = 1$, $h(x)$ is constant ($0$) because $1 \cdot \sin 1 \approx 0.84 < 1$, meaning $h(x)$ is differentiable at $x = 1$. However, $g(x)$ is not differentiable at $x = 1$. Thus, $f(x)$ is not differentiable at $x = 1$.
This gives $3$ points of non-differentiability: $-x_1, 1, x_1$. $\Rightarrow \beta = 3$.

Finally, $\alpha + \beta = 2 + 3 = 5$.

Answer: $5$

25952.text: Let $\alpha = \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{\infty}\sin^{2k}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$. Let $g: \left[0, 1\right] \to \mathbb{R}$ be the function defined by $g\left(x\right) = {2}^{ax} + {2}^{a\left(1 - x\right)}$. Then, which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
options: The function $g\left(x\right)$ attains its maximum at more than one point
The function $g\left(x\right)$ attains its minimum at more than one point
25952.sol:
Given,

$\alpha = \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{\infty}\sin^{2k}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$ and $g\left(x\right) = {2}^{ax} + {2}^{a\left(1 - x\right)}$.

Now solving,

$\alpha = \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{\infty}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{2k} = \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{\infty}{\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{k} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{4}}{1 - \dfrac{1}{4}} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Now putting the value of $\alpha$ in $g\left(x\right)$ we get,

$g\left(x\right) = 2\dfrac{x}{3} + 2\dfrac{\left(1 - x\right)}{3}$

Now, ${g}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{ln2}{3}\dfrac{\left({2}^{\dfrac{2x}{3}} - {2}^{\dfrac{1}{3}}\right)}{{2}^{\dfrac{x}{3}}}$

Now finding the critical point by ${g}^{'}\left(x\right) = 0$$⇒ x = \dfrac{1}{2}$

And, derivative changes sign from negative to positive at $x = \dfrac{1}{2}$, hence $x = \dfrac{1}{2}$ is point of local minimum as well as absolute minimum of $g\left(x\right)$ for $x \in \left[0, 1\right]$

Hence, minimum value of $g\left(x\right) = g\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

$= 2\dfrac{1}{6} + 2\dfrac{1}{6} = 2\dfrac{7}{6}$

$⇒$ Option $\left(A\right)$ is correct

Now maximum value of $g\left(x\right)$ is either equal to $g\left(0\right)$ or $g\left(1\right)$.

$g\left(0\right) = 1 + 2\dfrac{1}{3}$

$g\left(1\right) = 2\dfrac{1}{3} + 1$

Hence (B) and (C) are also correct.

26598.subject: Physics
26598.text: A rod of mass $m$ and length $L,$ pivoted at one of its ends, is hanging vertically. A bullet of the same mass moving at speed $v$ strikes the rod horizontally at a distance $x$ from its pivoted end and gets embedded in it. The combined system now rotates with an angular speed $\omega$ about the pivot. The maximum angular speed ${\omega}_{M}$ is achieved for $x = {x}_{M}$. Then
26598.sol:
The net torque on the system (rod+bullet) will be zero about hinge point. Therefore, we can apply the principle of angular momentum conservation about hinge point.

From angular momentum conservation,

$mvx = \left(\dfrac{m{L}^{2}}{3} + m{x}^{2}\right)\omega$

$⇒ \omega = \dfrac{3vx}{{L}^{2} + 3{x}^{2}} = \dfrac{3v}{\left(\dfrac{{L}^{2}}{x} + 3x\right)}$

For maximum angular velocity,

$\dfrac{d\omega}{dx} = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{{L}^{2}}{x} + 3x\right) = 0 ⇒ \dfrac{- {L}^{2}}{{x}^{2}} + 3 = 0 ⇒ x = \dfrac{L}{\sqrt{3}}$

$⇒ {\omega}_{max} = \dfrac{3v}{\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}{L}^{2}}{L} + \sqrt{3}L\right)} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}v}{2L}$

31262.text: Among $Fe^{2+}, Fe^{3+}, Cr^{2+}$ and $Zn^{2+}$, the ion that shows positive borax bead test and with highest ionisation enthalpy is:
31262.sol:
The borax bead test is given by transition metal ions that have unpaired electrons and form coloured compounds.

$Zn^{2+}$ has a completely filled $3d^{10}$ configuration, making it colourless, so it does not give a positive borax bead test.

The remaining ions and their electronic configurations are:
$Fe^{2+} : [Ar] 3d^{6}$
$Cr^{2+} : [Ar] 3d^{4}$
$Fe^{3+} : [Ar] 3d^{5}$

The ionisation enthalpy of an ion refers to the energy required to remove an electron from it. $Fe^{3+}$ has a highly stable half-filled $d$-subshell configuration ($3d^{5}$). Removing an electron from this stable configuration requires significantly more energy compared to removing an electron from $Fe^{2+}$ ($3d^{6}$) or $Cr^{2+}$ ($3d^{4}$).

Therefore, $Fe^{3+}$ shows a positive borax bead test and has the highest ionisation enthalpy among the given ions.

Answer: $Fe^{3+}$

32426.text:
Given below are the critical temperatures of some of the gases:

Gas Critical temperature $\left(K\right)$
$He$ $5 . 2$
${CH}_{4}$ $190$
${CO}_{2}$ $304 . 2$
${NH}_{3}$ $405 . 5$

The gas showing least adsorption on a definite amount of charcoal is
32426.sol:
The amount of gas adsorbed by a solid depends on the nature of gas. In general, easily liquefiable gases (i.e., with higher critical temperatures) are readily adsorbed as van der Waals’ forces are stronger near the critical temperatures. Thus, 1g of activated charcoal adsorbs more sulphur dioxide (critical temperature 630K), than methane (critical temperature 190K) which is still more than 4.5 mL of dihydrogen (critical temperature 33K).

So, more the critical temperature of gas greater is the ease of liquefaction hence greater is the adsorption.

Hence, among the given gases ammonia is adsorbed most and helium the least on definite amount of charcoal.

32634.text:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion $A$ and the other is labelled as Reason $R$

Assertion $A$ : The reduction of a metal oxide is easier if the metal formed is in liquid state than solid state.

Reason $R$ : The value of ${\Delta G}^{Θ}$ becomes more on negative side as entropy is higher in liquid state than solid state.

In the light of the above statements. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both $A$ and $R$ are correct and $R$ is the correct explanation of $A$
Both $A$ and $R$ are correct but $R$ is NOT the correct explanation of $A$
$A$ is correct but $R$ is not correct
$A$ is not correct but $R$ is correct
32634.sol:
The entropy is higher if the metal is in liquid state than when it is in solid state. The value of entropy change $( ∆ S )$ of the reduction process is more on positive side when the metal formed is in liquid state and the metal oxide being reduced is in solid state. Thus the value of ${∆}_{f}G$ becomes more on negative side and the reduction becomes easier.

$\Delta G = \Delta H - T \Delta S$

$∵$ Entropy of liquid is more than solid

$∴$ on melting the entropy increases and $\Delta G$ becomes more negative and hence it becomes easier to reduce metal.

34643.text: Let $y=y(x)$ be a differentiable function in the interval $(0, \infty)$ such that $y(1)=2$, and $\lim _{t \rightarrow x}\left(\frac{t^{2} y(x)-x^{2} y(t)}{x-t}\right)=3$ for each $x>0$. Then $2 y(2)$ is equal to
34643.sol:
Given the limit $\lim_{t \to x} \frac{t^2 y(x) - x^2 y(t)}{x - t} = 3$.
The limit is in $\frac{0}{0}$ form. Applying L'Hopital's Rule with respect to $t$:
$\lim_{t \to x} \frac{\frac{d}{dt}(t^2 y(x) - x^2 y(t))}{\frac{d}{dt}(x - t)} = 3$
$\lim_{t \to x} \frac{2t y(x) - x^2 y'(t)}{-1} = 3$
Substituting $t = x$:
$\frac{2x y(x) - x^2 y'(x)}{-1} = 3$
$x^2 y'(x) - 2x y(x) = 3$
Dividing by $x^4$ to make it a linear differential equation or recognizing the quotient rule form:
$\frac{x^2 y'(x) - 2x y(x)}{x^4} = \frac{3}{x^4}$
$\frac{d}{dx} \left( \frac{y(x)}{x^2} \right) = \frac{3}{x^4}$
Integrating both sides with respect to $x$:
$\frac{y(x)}{x^2} = \int 3x^{-4} dx = \frac{3x^{-3}}{-3} + C = -\frac{1}{x^3} + C$
Given $y(1) = 2$:
$\frac{2}{1^2} = -\frac{1}{1^3} + C \implies 2 = -1 + C \implies C = 3$
So, $\frac{y(x)}{x^2} = -\frac{1}{x^3} + 3$
$y(x) = -\frac{1}{x} + 3x^2$
We need to find $2y(2)$:
$y(2) = -\frac{1}{2} + 3(2^2) = -\frac{1}{2} + 12 = \frac{23}{2}$
$2y(2) = 2 \times \frac{23}{2} = 23$

Length of L.R.$= \dfrac{2{b}^{2}}{a} = \dfrac{2 \times 1}{a}$

Given length of L.R. of $E$ and $H$ are equal

So $\dfrac{2}{a} = 3 ⇒ a = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Now ${e}_{H} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{b}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} + 1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{{\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)}^{2}}} + 1 ⇒ {e}_{H} = \sqrt{\dfrac{9}{4} + 1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{13}{4}}$

36548.text: Let S be a set of 5 elements and $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{S})$ denote the power set of S. Let E be an event of choosing an ordered pair ($\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}$) from the set $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{S}) \times \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{S})$ such that $\mathrm{A} \cap \mathrm{B}=\emptyset$. If the probability of the event $E$ is $\frac{3^{p}}{2^{q}}$, where $p, q \in N$, then $p+q$ is equal to $\_\_\_\_$
36548.sol:
$S$ has 5 elements, so $P(S)$ has $2^5 = 32$ subsets.
Total ordered pairs from $P(S) \times P(S)$ is $32^2 = 1024$
For pairs $(A, B)$ with $A \cap B = \emptyset$: each of the 5 elements has 3 choices - in $A$ only, in $B$ only, or in neither
Number of favorable outcomes = $3^5 = 243$
Probability $= \frac{243}{1024} = \frac{3^5}{2^{10}}$
With $p = 5$ and $q = 10$, we get $p + q = 15$

37378.text:
Let $\mathrm{A}=\{0,1,2, \ldots, 9\}$. Let R be a relation on A defined by $(x, y) \in \mathrm{R}$ if and only if $|x-y|$ is a multiple of 3. Given below are two statements:
Statement I: $n(\mathrm{R})=36$.
Statement II: $R$ is an equivalence relation.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
37378.sol:
The relation $R$ on $A = \{0,1,2,\ldots,9\}$ is defined by $(x,y) \in R$ iff $|x-y|$ is a multiple of 3, i.e., $x \equiv y \pmod{3}$.
Statement II:
$R$ is reflexive ($|x-x|=0$, a multiple of 3), symmetric ($|x-y|=|y-x|$), and transitive (if $x \equiv y$ and $y \equiv z \pmod{3}$, then $x \equiv z \pmod{3}$). So $R$ is an equivalence relation. Statement II is correct.
Statement I:
The equivalence classes are $\{0,3,6,9\}$ (4 elements), $\{1,4,7\}$ (3 elements), $\{2,5,8\}$ (3 elements).
$n(R) = 4^2 + 3^2 + 3^2 = 16 + 9 + 9 = 34 \neq 36$. Statement I is incorrect.

39531.subject: Physics
39531.text:
A cylindrical conductor of length 2 m and area of cross-section $0.2 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$ carries an electric current of 1.6 A when its ends are connected to a 2 V battery. Mobility of electrons in the conductor is $\alpha \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}^{2} / V. s$. The value of $\alpha$ is :
(electron concentration $=5 \times 10^{28} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$ and electron charge $\left.=1.6 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{C}\right)$
39531.sol:
For a cylindrical conductor with length 2 m, cross-section 0.2 mm² = 0.2 × 10⁻⁶ m², carrying 1.6 A at 2 V.
Resistance: $R = V/I = 2/1.6 = 1.25$ Ω.
Resistivity: $\rho = RA/L = 1.25 \times 0.2 \times 10^{-6}/2$
$= 0.125 \times 10^{-6}$ Ω·m.
Using $\rho = 1/(ne\mu)$, mobility: $\mu = 1/(ne\rho)$
$= 1/(5 \times 10^{28} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 0.125 \times 10^{-6})$
$= 1/(1 \times 10^3) = 10^{-3}$ m²/V·s.
Thus $\alpha = 1$.

42252.subject: Physics
42252.text: A ball is released from a height $h$. If ${t}_{1}$ and ${t}_{2}$ be the time required to complete first half and second half of the distance respectively. Then, choose the correct relation between ${t}_{1}$ and ${t}_{2}$.
42252.sol:
As the body is dropped from a certain height $h$, its initial velocity will be zero.

For first half, ${h}_{1} = \dfrac{h}{2}$.

Using second equation of motion, $s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}a{t}^{2}$

We have, $\dfrac{h}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}g{t}_{1}^{2}$.

Time taken in travel first half of the height, ${t}_{1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{h}{g}} . . . \left(1\right)$.

For total height $h$, using again second equation of motion,

$h = \dfrac{1}{2}g{\left({t}_{1} + {t}_{2}\right)}^{2} ⇒ \left({t}_{1} + {t}_{2}\right) = \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}} . . . \left(2\right)$

From equation $\left(1\right)$ and $\left(2\right)$,

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{{t}_{1}}{{t}_{1} + {t}_{2}}$

$⇒ 1 + \dfrac{{t}_{2}}{{t}_{1}} = \sqrt{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{t}_{1}}{{t}_{2}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2} - 1}$

Thus, the relation is ${t}_{2} = \left(\sqrt{2} - 1\right){t}_{1}$.

44050.subject: Physics
44050.text: If $\epsilon, E$ and $t$ represent the free space permittivity, electric field and time respectively, then the unit of $\frac{\epsilon E}{t}$ will be :
44050.sol:
We need to find the unit of $\frac{\epsilon E}{t}$.
From Maxwell's equations, the displacement current density is given by $J_d = \epsilon \frac{\partial E}{\partial t}$.
The term $\frac{\epsilon E}{t}$ has the same dimensions as displacement current density $J_d$.
Current density $J$ is defined as current per unit area, $J = \frac{I}{A}$.
The SI unit of current $I$ is Ampere (A) and the SI unit of area $A$ is $m^2$.
Therefore, the unit of current density is $A/m^2$.
Alternatively, using dimensions:
$[\epsilon] = M^{-1}L^{-3}T^4A^2$
$[E] = MLT^{-3}A^{-1}$
$[t] = T$
Dimension of $\frac{\epsilon E}{t} = \frac{(M^{-1}L^{-3}T^4A^2)(MLT^{-3}A^{-1})}{T} = L^{-2}A$.
This corresponds to the unit $A/m^2$.

It is given that

$n \times {10}^{- 5} = 462 \times {10}^{- 5} ⇒ n = 462$

45284.subject: Botany
45284.text: Most accepted theory for ascent of sap is
45284.sol: Transpiration pull is the tension which develops due to transpiration. It has been demonstrated and evidenced, that rate of water absorption and hence, ascent of sap closely follows the rate of transpiration and hence, ascent of sap closely follows the rate of transpiration.Cohesion andtranspiration pull theory, given by Dixon and Jolly (1894) is the most accepted theory for ascent of sap.Root Pressure theory (Priestley; 1916) is a manifestation of active water absorption. It was objected, as it has not been applicable to all plants (eg, gymnospermous tallest trees). Moreover, this pressure is low to raise the sap to the top of trees and also many reasons which this theory was unable to proove.Pulsation theory orvital force theory (J C Bose; 1923) was also discarded because living cells do not seen to be involved in the ascent of sap as water continuous to rise upward in the plant in which roots have been cut or living cells of stem are killed by poison and heat (Strassburger; 1891).Capillarity theory (Bohm; 1863), laid stress on capillarity movement of water due to adhesion and cohesion forces balanced by downward pull of gravity. It was also discarded, as the value of capillary is too small and applicable only to small sized plants and tall plants with narrow vessels.

45287.subject: Botany
45287.text: The rupture and fractionation do not usually occur in the water column in vessel/tracheids during the ascent of sap because of
45287.sol:
The vertical conduction of water from root to aerial parts of plant is called ascent of sap. The water molecules remain joined to each other due to a force of attraction called cohesion force. This attraction is due to the presence of hydrogen bonds between them. The magnitude of this force is very high therefore, the continuous water column in the xylem cannot be broken easily due to the force of gravity or other obstructions offered by internal tissues in the upward movement of water. This adhesive property of water, i.e., attraction between the water molecules and the walls of xylem ensures the continuity of water column in the xylem.
Due to transpiration water evaporates to outer atmosphere through stomata. As a result leaf cells develop low water potential and water from leaf veins moves into leaf cells. The xylem vessel in turn draw water from xylem of main stem. A pressure (pull) is thus, exerted by all the leaves on the stems, which is called transpiration pull. This is strong enough to pull up the column of water to a great height.

Now, angle turned in 6 s from the starting

Angle turned between $t=3 \mathrm{~s}$ to $t=6 \mathrm{~s}\theta_{\text{lost }}=\theta_2-\theta_3=80 \pi-20 \pi=60 \pi$

46740.text: A closed organ pipe of length 20 cm is sounded with tuning fork in resonance. What is the frequency of tuning fork? $(v=332 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s})$
46740.sol: Key Idea : When length of air column is $\frac{\lambda}{4}$, then first resonance occurs. If we adjust the length of air-column in closed organ pipe as such its any natural frequency equals to the frequency of tuning fork, then the amplitude of forced vibrations of air-column increases very much. This is the state of resonance. At first resonance $l=\frac{\lambda}{4}$ So, frequency of tuning fork $f=\frac{v}{\lambda}=\frac{v}{4 l}$ Given, $l=20 \mathrm{~cm}=0.2 \mathrm{~m}, v=332 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ Hence, $f=\frac{332}{4 \times 0.2}=415 \mathrm{~Hz}$

51703.text: On a rectangular hyperbola $x^{2} - y^{2} = a^{2}, a > 0,$ three points $A, B, C$ are taken as follows $: A = \left(- a, 0\right); B$ and $C$ are placed symmetrically with respect to the $X$-axis on the branch of the hyperbola not containing $A$. Suppose that the $\Delta ABC$ is equilateral. If the side length of the $\Delta ABC$ is $ka,$ then $k$ lies in the interval
51703.sol:
We have rectangular hyperbola

$x^{2} - y^{2} = a^{2}$

Given $ABC$ is an equilateral triangle.

$∴AB = BC = AC$

$AB^{2} = BC^{2}$

$a^{2}\left(sec\theta + 1\right){}^{2} + a^{2}\tan^{2}\theta = 4a^{2}\tan^{2}\theta$

$⇒ \left(sec\theta + 1\right){}^{2} = 3\tan^{2}\theta$

$⇒ \left(sec\theta +1\right){}^{2} = 3 \left(\sec^{2}\theta -$1\right)$

$⇒ $\left(sec\theta +1\right)${}^{2} = 3 \lleft(sec\theta +1\\right)\lleft(sec\theta -1\right)$

$⇒ sec\theta +1 = 3sec\theta -3$

$⇒ sec\theta =2$

$⇒ \theta =60 °$

$∵$ Side $BC = 2atan\theta$

$= 2atan60 ° = $2a\sqrt{3}$

But side of triangle is $ka$.

$∴ka = $2a\sqrt{3}$

$k = $2\sqrt{3}$

Hence, $k \in (2,4]$

52279.text: Consider the wall of a dam to be straight with height $H$ and length $L$. It holds a lake of water of height $h  \left(h < H\right)$ on one side. Let the density of water be ${ρ}_{w}$ Denote the torque about the axis along the bottom length of the wall by ${τ}_{1}$. Denote also a similar torque due to the water up to height $h / 2$ and wall length $L / 2$ by ${τ}_{2}$. Then, ${τ}_{1} / {τ}_{2} (ignore atmospheric pressure) is$
52279.sol:
Consider a strip of width $dy$ at a depth $\left(h - y\right)$ below the surface. 

Torque on bottom length ( $OZ$ in diagram) due to force of water on strip of width $dy$ is 

$dτ =$ Force $\times$ Perpendicular distance $=$ Pressure $\times$ Area $\times$ Distance

$dτ = ρg\left(h - y\right) \cdot \left(L \cdot dy\right) \cdot y$

So, torque on bottom length due to complete volume of water, 

${τ}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{h}Lρg\left(h - y\right)y \cdot dy$

$= Lρg\left[{∫}_{0}^{h}\left(hy - {y}^{2}\right)dy\right]$

$= Lρg{\left[\dfrac{h{y}^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{{y}^{3}}{3}\right]}_{0}^{h}$

$= Lρg\left[\dfrac{{h}^{3}}{2} - \dfrac{{h}^{3}}{3}\right]$

or ${τ}_{1} = \dfrac{Lρg{h}^{3}}{6} . . . ( i )$

and torque due to water upto height $\dfrac{h}{2}$ and wall length $\dfrac{1}{2}$, ${τ}_{2} = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{h}{2}}\dfrac{L}{2}ρg\left(\dfrac{h}{2} - y\right)ydy$

$= \dfrac{L}{2}ρg{\left[\left(\dfrac{h{y}^{2}}{4} - \dfrac{h{y}^{3}}{3}\right)\right]}_{0}^{h}$

$= \dfrac{L}{2}ρg\left[\dfrac{{h}^{3}}{16} - \dfrac{{h}^{3}}{24}\right] = \dfrac{Lρg{h}^{3}}{16 \times 6}$

So, $\dfrac{{τ}_{1}}{{τ}_{2}} = 16$

55990.text: If time required for 90 % completion of a first order reaction is '$t$'. What is the time required for 99.9 % completion of reaction at same temperature?
55990.sol:
For a first order reaction, the time required for completion is given by $t = \dfrac{2.303}{k} \log \left( \dfrac{a}{a-x} \right)

For 90\%$ completion, $x = 0.9a$

$t_{90\%} = \dfrac{2.303}{k} \log \left( \dfrac{a}{a - 0.9a} \right) = \dfrac{2.303}{k} \log10 = \dfrac{2.303}{k}

Given $ t_{90\%} = t$, so $t = $\dfrac{2.303}{k}

For 99.9\%$ completion, $x = 0.999a$

Substituting the value of $t$, we get $t_{99.9\%} = 3t$

60564.subject: Mathematics
60564.text: Area enclosed by curve $y = 2x^2$ and lines $x \geq 1,\ y \leq 4$ is..... sq. units
60564.sol:
The region is bounded by the curve $y = 2x^2$, the vertical line $x = 1$, and the horizontal line $y = 4$.

The intersection of $y = 2x^2$ and $y = 4$ in the region $x \geq 1$ is given by:

$2x^2 = 4 \Rightarrow x^2 = 2 \Rightarrow x = \sqrt{2}$

The required area $A$ is the integral of the upper boundary minus the lower boundary from $x = 1$ to $x = \sqrt{2}$:

$A = \int_{1}^{\sqrt{2}} (4 - 2x^2) dx$

$A = \left[ 4x - \dfrac{2x^3}{3} \right]_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}$

$A = \left( 4\sqrt{2} - \dfrac{4\sqrt{2}}{3} \right) - \left( 4 - \dfrac{2}{3} \right)$

$A = \dfrac{8\sqrt{2}}{3} - \dfrac{10}{3} = \dfrac{8\sqrt{2} - 10}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{8\sqrt{2}-10}{3}$

61313.subject: Mathematics
61313.text: The solution of the differential equation. $(1+x) \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{d} x}-x \mathrm{y}=1-x$ is
options: $\mathrm{y}(1+x)=x+\mathrm{ce}^x$, where c is the constant of integration
$\mathrm{y}(1+x)=\mathrm{ce}^x$, where c is the constant of integration
$\mathrm{y}(1-x)=x-\mathrm{ce}^x$, where c is the constant of integration
$\mathrm{y}(1+x)=x \mathrm{ce}^{-x}$, where c is the constant of integration
61313.sol:
Convert the differential equation to standard form by dividing through by $1+x$:

$\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} - \frac{x}{1+x}y = \frac{1-x}{1+x}$

Identify $P(x) = -\frac{x}{1+x}$ and compute the integrating factor:

$\int P(x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \int \left(-1 + \frac{1}{1+x}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x = -x + \ln|1+x|$

$\text{IF} = e^{-x + \ln|1+x|} = (1+x)e^{-x}$

Multiply through by the integrating factor and integrate:

$y(1+x)e^{-x} = \int (1-x)e^{-x}\,\mathrm{d}x + C$

Evaluate the integral using integration by parts with $u = 1-x$, $\mathrm{d}v = e^{-x}\,\mathrm{d}x$:

$\int (1-x)e^{-x}\,\mathrm{d}x = (1-x)(-e^{-x}) - \int (-e^{-x})(-\mathrm{d}x) = -(1-x)e^{-x} - e^{-x} = xe^{-x}$

Substitute back and solve for $y$:

$y(1+x)e^{-x} = xe^{-x} + C$

$y(1+x) = x + Ce^x$

This matches option A.

Differentiating the given equation with respect to $x$:

$e^0 + 0 \cdot e^0 \left(0 + 0 \cdot \dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) = \dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2 \sin 0 \cos 0$

$1 + 0 = \dfrac{dy}{dx} + 0$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1$

Answer: $1$

62005.text: If $e^x + e^{f(x)} = e$, then the domain of $f(x)$ is
62005.sol:
Given $e^x + e^{f(x)} = e$

$e^{f(x)} = e - e^x$

Taking natural logarithm on both sides, we get

$f(x) = \ln(e - e^x)$

For $f(x)$ to be defined, the argument of the logarithm must be strictly positive.

$e - e^x > 0$

$e^x < e$

$x < 1$

Therefore, the domain of $f(x)$ is $(-\infty, 1)$.

Answer: $(-\infty, 1)$

62201.text: If $\mathrm{A}=\left[\begin{array}{lll}\mathrm{a} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \mathrm{ b} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \mathrm{c}\end{array}\right]$ where $\mathrm{a}=7^{\mathrm{x}}, \mathrm{b}=7^{7^x}, \mathrm{c}=7^{7^{7^x}}$ then $\int|A| \mathrm{d} x$, (Where $|A|$ is the determinant of the matrix $A$ ) is equal to
options: $\frac{7^{7^{7^x}}}{\log 7}+\mathrm{k}, \quad$ where k is constant of integration
$\frac{7^{7^{7^x}}}{(\log 7)^3}+\mathrm{k} \quad, \quad$ where k is constant of integration
$7^{7^{7^x}}(\log 7)^3+\mathrm{k}, \quad$ where k is constant of integration
62201.sol:
Determinant Evaluation: The determinant of the diagonal matrix $A$ is the product of its diagonal elements: $|A| = a \cdot b \cdot c = 7^x \cdot 7^{7^x} \cdot 7^{7^{7^x}}$.

Integral Setup: The required integral is $\int |A| dx = \int 7^x \cdot 7^{7^x} \cdot 7^{7^{7^x}} dx$.

Substitution: Let $u = 7^{7^{7^x}}$.
Differentiating using the chain rule: $\frac{du}{dx} = 7^{7^{7^x}} \ln 7 \cdot \frac{d}{dx}(7^{7^x}) = 7^{7^{7^x}} \ln 7 \cdot (7^{7^x} \ln 7 \cdot 7^x \ln 7) = 7^{7^{7^x}} \cdot 7^{7^x} \cdot 7^x \cdot (\ln 7)^3$.
This gives $dx = \frac{du}{u \cdot 7^{7^x} \cdot 7^x \cdot (\ln 7)^3}$.

Integration: Substituting into the integral yields $\int u \cdot \frac{du}{u \cdot (\ln 7)^3} = \frac{1}{(\ln 7)^3} \int du = \frac{u}{(\ln 7)^3} + k$.

Replacing $u$ gives the result $\frac{7^{7^{7^x}}}{(\ln 7)^3} + k$.

Answer Selection: This matches option C, interpreting $\log 7$ as $\ln 7$.

64094.subject: Mathematics
64094.text: If $a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots, a_n$ are in arithmetic progression with common difference d, then $\tan\left[\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{d}{1 + a_1 a_2}\right) + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{d}{1 + a_2 a_3}\right) + \ldots + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{d}{1 + a_{n-1} a_n}\right)\right] = $ ____
64094.sol:
Given $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$ are in arithmetic progression with common difference $d$.

$d = a_2 - a_1 = a_3 - a_2 = \ldots = a_n - a_{n-1}$

The general term of the series is:

$\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{d}{1 + a_k a_{k+1}}\right) = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{a_{k+1} - a_k}{1 + a_k a_{k+1}}\right)$

Using the identity $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x - y}{1 + xy}\right) = \tan^{-1} x - \tan^{-1} y$, we get:

$\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{a_{k+1} - a_k}{1 + a_k a_{k+1}}\right) = \tan^{-1} a_{k+1} - \tan^{-1} a_k$

Let $S$ be the sum of the inverse trigonometric series:

$S = \sum_{k=1}^{n-1} \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{d}{1 + a_k a_{k+1}}\right)$

$S = (\tan^{-1} a_2 - \tan^{-1} a_1) + (\tan^{-1} a_3 - \tan^{-1} a_2) + \ldots + (\tan^{-1} a_n - \tan^{-1} a_{n-1})$

This is a telescoping sum, which simplifies to:

$S = \tan^{-1} a_n - \tan^{-1} a_1$

Applying the inverse tangent difference formula:

$S = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{a_n - a_1}{1 + a_1 a_n}\right)$

The given expression is $\tan(S)$:

$\tan(S) = \tan\left[\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{a_n - a_1}{1 + a_1 a_n}\right)\right] = \dfrac{a_n - a_1}{1 + a_1 a_n}$

Two point charges $+10 \mu \mathrm{C}$ and 4 \mu$\mathrm{C}$ are placed 10 cm apart in air. The work required to be done to bring them 2 cm closer is
$\left(\frac{1}{4 \pi \epsilon_0}=9 \times 10^9 \text{ SI units }\right)$
67038.sol:
The work done to bring two point charges closer equals the change in their electrostatic potential energy. The potential energy $U$ for point charges $q_1$ and $q_2$ separated by distance $r$ is $U = \frac{1}{4 \pi \epsilon_0} \frac{q_1 q_2}{r}$.

Given $q_1 = +10 \mu\mathrm{C} = 10 \times 10^{-6}\ \mathrm{C}$, $q_2 = +4 \mu\mathrm{C} = 4 \times 10^{-6}\ \mathrm{C}$, with $\frac{1}{4 \pi \epsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^9\ \mathrm{N\ m^2/C^2}$.
Initial separation $r_1 = 0.10\ \mathrm{m}$, final separation $r_2 = 0.08\ \mathrm{m}$ after moving $2\ \mathrm{cm}$ closer.

The work $W$ equals the difference in potential energy: $W = U_2 - U_1$.

Using $U = k \frac{q_1 q_2}{r}$ with $k = 9 \times 10^9$:
$U_1 = \frac{(9 \times 10^9)(10 \times 10^{-6})(4 \times 10^{-6})}{0.10} = 3.6\ \mathrm{J}$
$U_2 = \frac{(9 \times 10^9)(10 \times 10^{-6})(4 \times 10^{-6})}{0.08} = 4.5\ \mathrm{J}$

The work done is $W = 4.5 - 3.6 = 0.9\ \mathrm{J}$.

Alternatively, applying the direct formula:
$W = k q_1 q_2 \left( \frac{1}{r_2} - \frac{1}{r_1} \right) = (9 \times 10^9)(40 \times 10^{-12}) \left( \frac{1}{0.08} - \frac{1}{0.10} \right) = 0.9\ \mathrm{J}$.

Final Answer: $\boxed{0.9\ \mathrm{J}}$
67038.meta: Two point charges +10 μ C and 4 μ C are placed 10 cm apart in air. The work required to be done to bring them 2 cm closer is ((1)/(4 π ε_0)=9 × 10^9 SI units )

68606.text: Two radioactive materials ' $M_1{ }^{\prime}$ and ' $M_2{ }^{\prime}$ have decay constants ' $9 \lambda$ ' and ' $\lambda$ ' respectively. Initially they have the same number of nuclei. 68606.sol:
Given initial nuclei count $N_0$ for both materials, their quantities follow exponential decay: $N_1(t) = N_0 e^{-9\lambda t}$ for $M_1$ and $N_2(t) = N_0 e^{-\lambda t}$ for $M_2$, where $t$ is time.

Equating exponents gives $-8\lambda t = -1$, so $t = \frac{1}{8\lambda}$.

The ratio becomes $\frac{1}{e}$ at time $t = \frac{1}{8\lambda}$, corresponding to option D.

69738.text: The length of steel rod is 5 cm longer than the copper rod at all temperatures. The length of the steel and copper rod is respectively (Coefficient of linear expansion for steel and copper is respectively $1.1 \times 10^{-5} /{ }^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ and $1.7 \times 10^{-5} /{ }^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ )
69738.sol:
The constant length difference condition $L_s(T) - L_c(T) = 5\text{cm}$ must hold for all temperatures. Applying thermal expansion formulas $L(T) = L_0(1 + \alpha\Delta T)$ yields:

$(L_s - L_c) + (L_s\alpha_s - L_c\alpha_c)\Delta T = 5$

For temperature independence, both $L_s - L_c = 5$ and $L_s\alpha_s = L_c\alpha_c$ must be satisfied.

Substituting $L_s = L_c + 5$ into the second equation:

$(L_c + 5)\alpha_s = L_c\alpha_c$

$L_c = \frac{5\alpha_s}{\alpha_c - \alpha_s} = \frac{5 \times 1.1 \times 10^{-5}}{(1.7 - 1.1) \times 10^{-5}} = \frac{5.5}{0.6} \approx 9.17\text{cm}$

Thus $L_s = L_c + 5 \approx 14.17\text{cm}$.

These values correspond to nearly 14 cm and 9 cm, matching option B.

70178.subject: Physics
70178.text: A single slit diffraction pattern is formed with white light. For what wavelength of light the $4^{\text{th }}$ secondary maximum in diffraction pattern coincides with the $3^{\text{rd }}$ secondary maximum in the pattern of light of wavelength ' $\lambda$ ' ?
70178.sol:
To determine the condition for secondary maxima coincidence in single-slit diffraction, use the general formula $a \sin \theta = (n + \frac{1}{2}) \lambda$, where $a$ is the slit width, $\theta$ is the diffraction angle, $n$ is the order (starting at $n=1$ for the first secondary maximum), and $\lambda$ is the wavelength.

For the $4^{\text{th}}$ secondary maximum of wavelength $\lambda'$ at angle $\theta_1$:
$a \sin \theta_1 = (4 + \frac{1}{2}) \lambda' = \frac{9}{2} \lambda'$

For the $3^{\text{rd}}$ secondary maximum of wavelength $\lambda$ at angle $\theta_2$:
$a \sin \theta_2 = (3 + \frac{1}{2}) \lambda = \frac{7}{2} \lambda$

Since the angular positions coincide, $\sin \theta_1 = \sin \theta_2$, equating the two expressions:
$\frac{9}{2} \lambda' = \frac{7}{2} \lambda$

Multiply both sides by 2:
$9 \lambda' = 7 \lambda$

Solve for $\lambda'$:
$\lambda' = \frac{7}{9} \lambda$

The wavelength for which the $4^{\text{th}}$ secondary maximum coincides with the $3^{\text{rd}}$ secondary maximum of wavelength $\lambda$ is $\frac{7 \lambda}{9}$.

The option is B.

Match List I with List II

(C). Klinefelter's syndrome(III). 21^{st}$ Trisomy

71381.sol:
Thalassemia is an autosomal recessive blood disorder, which is classified as a Mendelian disorder. Thus, (A) matches with (IV).

Turner's syndrome is caused by the absence of one of the X chromosomes, resulting in a karyotype of $45$, X0, which is an X-monosomy. Thus, (B) matches with (I).

Klinefelter's syndrome is caused by the presence of an additional copy of the X-chromosome, resulting in a karyotype of $47$, XXY. Thus, (C) matches with (II).

Down's syndrome is caused by the presence of an additional copy of chromosome number $21$, known as $21^{st}$ Trisomy. Thus, (D) matches with (III).

The correct matching is (A) - (IV), (B) - (I), (C) - (II), (D) - (III).

Answer: (A) - (IV), (B) - (I), (C) - (II), (D) - (III)

72628.subject: General Ability
72628.text:
In this section each item consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences in each have been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. You are required to find the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark your response accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

S1. Liberalisation and globalisation freed India's economy from the low GDP trap that had impeded India's progress
S6. Today India has transformed into one of the largest economies of the world
P. India's 3 pc rate of growth and a set of emergent circumstances led to a balance of payment crisis in the early 1990s
Q. Ease of business was ensured, and the requirement for import licences, and production quotas, were removed
R. Apart from these measures India also took a loan from the IMF to tide over the crisis, but after 1993, India has not taken another loan from the IMF
S. In a landmark budget in 1991, responding to the emergent crisis, India delicenced many industries and liberalised its economic policies
72628.sol:
Sentence S1 introduces the topic of liberalisation freeing India's economy from a low GDP trap.

Sentence P logically follows S1 by detailing the historical context of this low GDP trap, explaining that a low growth rate and emergent circumstances led to a balance of payment crisis in the early 1990s.

Sentence S must follow P because it explicitly refers back to 'the emergent crisis' introduced in P and describes the initial response of delicencing and liberalising in the 1991 budget.

Sentence Q elaborates on the specific liberalisation policies mentioned in S, such as ensuring ease of business and removing import licences and production quotas.

Sentence R logically follows Q by using the transition phrase 'Apart from these measures' to introduce an additional step taken to manage the crisis, which was taking an IMF loan.

Sentence S6 naturally concludes the passage by stating the present-day result of these historical actions.

Therefore, the logically coherent sequence is P S Q R.

73812.subject: General Ability
73812.text:
A light ray is falling on a face of an equilateral glass prism as shown in the figure:

Which one of the following diagrams correctly shows the complete path of the ray through the glass prism?
73812.sol:
When the light ray falls perpendicularly on the first face of the equilateral glass prism, its angle of incidence is $0^{\circ}$. Thus, it enters the prism undeviated.

In the triangle formed at the top vertex, the angle of the prism is $60^{\circ}$, and the angle at the first face is $90^{\circ}$. The angle between the ray inside the prism and the second face is $180^{\circ} - (90^{\circ} + 60^{\circ}) = 30^{\circ}$.

The normal to the second face makes an angle of $90^{\circ}$ with the surface. The angle of incidence at the second face is $90^{\circ} - 30^{\circ} = 60^{\circ}$.

The critical angle for a glass-air interface is approximately $42^{\circ}$. Since the angle of incidence ($60^{\circ}$) is greater than the critical angle, the ray undergoes total internal reflection.

By the law of reflection, the angle of reflection is $60^{\circ}$, so the reflected ray makes an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with the second face.

In the triangle formed by the reflected ray, the second face, and the base, the prism's rightmost angle is $60^{\circ}$. The angle the ray makes with the second face is $30^{\circ}$. Therefore, the angle at which the ray strikes the base is $180^{\circ} - (60^{\circ} + 30^{\circ}) = 90^{\circ}$.

Since the reflected ray strikes the base perpendicularly, its angle of incidence at the base is $0^{\circ}$, and it emerges from the prism undeviated.

This complete path is correctly represented in the diagram corresponding to option (4).

76787.subject: Mathematics
76787.text:
Passage: Let $\displaystyle\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{a\sin x+b\cos x}{(a+b)(\sin x+\cos x)}\,dx=k$.

Question: What is the value of $k$ ?
76787.sol:
Let $I = \int_0^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{a\sin x+b\cos x}{(a+b)(\sin x+\cos x)}\,dx$

Using the property $\int_0^a f(x)\,dx = \int_0^a f(a-x)\,dx$, we get:

$I = \int_0^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{a\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-x\right)+b\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-x\right)}{(a+b)\left(\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-x\right)+\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-x\right)\right)}\,dx$

$I = \int_0^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{a\cos x+b\sin x}{(a+b)(\cos x+\sin x)}\,dx$

Adding the two equations for $I$, we get:

$2I = \int_0^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{a\sin x+b\cos x+a\cos x+b\sin x}{(a+b)(\sin x+\cos x)}\,dx$

$2I = \int_0^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{(a+b)(\sin x+\cos x)}{(a+b)(\sin x+\cos x)}\,dx$

$2I = \int_0^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}} 1 \,dx$

$2I = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$I = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

Thus, $k = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$

77980.text:
Under which of the following conditions may binomial distribution be used?
I. The number of trials is infinite and not fixed.
II. The trials are independent.
III. Each trial has two possible outcomes.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
77980.sol:
The conditions for a binomial distribution are:

1. The number of trials is finite and fixed.

2. The trials are independent of each other.

3. Each trial has exactly two mutually exclusive outcomes, often termed as success and failure.

4. The probability of success remains constant for each trial.

Statement I is incorrect because the number of trials must be finite and fixed.

Statement II is correct because the trials must be independent.

Statement III is correct because each trial must have exactly two possible outcomes.

Therefore, only conditions II and III are correct.

Answer: II and III

The main functions include the attachment of sister chromatids, and it is the site for attachment of spindle fibre. Centromeres help in the proper alignment and segregation of the chromosomes during the process of cell division in eukaryotic cells.

The main component of the centromere is the kinetochore and DNA associated proteins. Centromeres are densely packed with the heterogeneous domain capped by the trilaminar kinetochore. 84709.subject: Zoology
84709.text:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the skeletal muscle?

A. Muscle bundles are held together by collagenous tissue layer called fascicle.

B. Sarcoplasmic reticulum of muscle fibre is a store house of calcium ions.

C. Striated appearance of skeletal muscle fibre is due to distribution pattern of actin and myosin proteins.

D. M line is considered as functional unit of contraction called sarcomere.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
84709.sol:
Muscle fascicles are held together by a common collagenous connective tissue layer called ligament.

The sarcoplasmic reticulum in the muscle fibers resembles a network of smooth endoplasmic reticulums. This Sarcoplasmic reticulum functions as a storehouse of calcium iron.

The striated appearance of the skeletal muscle fibre is a result of the distribution pattern of proteins myosin and actin. The sarcomere is responsible for the striated appearance of muscle. The actin is a thin filament and myosin is a thick filament.

M line contains the protein called myomesin, and it marks the centre of the sarcomere. A sarcomere is the functional unit (contractile unit) of a muscle fiber.

Hence, the most appropriate answer is option C, i.e., B and C only.

86787.subject: Physics
86787.text: Ice on land mass melting into ocean, due to global warming, is estimated to be around $1.3 \times 10^{15}$ kg per year. The density of sea water is $1025$ kg\cdot m^{-3}$. Assuming that the melting rate of ice remains constant and the effective surface area covered by the oceans is 3.6 \times 10^{14}$ m^2$, the estimated average rise in sea level (in m) in the next $75 years will be closest to
86787.sol:
Total mass of ice melted in $75$ years is given by:

$M = 1.3 \times 10^{15} \times 75 = 97.5 \times 10^{15}$ kg

The volume of sea water added to the oceans is:

$V = \dfrac{M}{\rho} = \dfrac{97.5 \times 10^{15}}{1025}$ m$^3$

The average rise in sea level is the volume added divided by the effective surface area of the oceans:

$h = \dfrac{V}{A} = \dfrac{97.5 \times 10^{15}}{1025 \times 3.6 \times 10^{14}}$

$h = \dfrac{975}{3690} \approx 0.264$ m

The estimated average rise in sea level is closest to $0.25$ m.

Answer: $0.25$

100029.subject: Physics
100029.text: The heat dissipated in a resistance wire is given by Joule's law of heating, $H = I^2 R t$. In an experiment, the maximum percentage errors in the measurement of heat dissipated ($H$), resistance ($R$), and time ($t$) are $9\%$, $2\%$, and $1\%$ respectively. The percentage error in the measurement of current ($I$) is:
100029.sol:
The formula for heat dissipated is $H = I^2 R t$.

The maximum percentage error in $H$ is given by the sum of the percentage errors of its factors, multiplied by their respective powers:
$\dfrac{\Delta H}{H} \times 100 = 2 \left( \dfrac{\Delta I}{I} \times 100 \right) + \left( \dfrac{\Delta R}{R} \times 100 \right) + \left( \dfrac{\Delta t}{t} \times 100 \right)$

Given the percentage errors:
$\dfrac{\Delta H}{H} \times 100 = 9\%$
$\dfrac{\Delta R}{R} \times 100 = 2\%$
$\dfrac{\Delta t}{t} \times 100 = 1\%$

Substitute these values into the error equation:
$9\% = 2 \left( \dfrac{\Delta I}{I} \times 100 \right) + 2\% + 1\%$

$9\% = 2 \left( \dfrac{\Delta I}{I} \times 100 \right) + 3\%$

$2 \left( \dfrac{\Delta I}{I} \times 100 \right) = 9\% - 3\% = 6\%$

$\dfrac{\Delta I}{I} \times 100 = \dfrac{6\%}{2} = 3\%$

The percentage error in the measurement of current is $3\%$.

Answer: $3\%$

100427.text:
Assertion (A) The speed of a body in uniform circular motion is constant.

Reason $(R)$ In uniform circular motion, the acceleration of the body is constant.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
100427.sol:
(i) Assertion is correct : In uniform circular motion, body moves with constant speed. It is magnitude of velocity, which is constant.
(ii) Reason is incorrect : In uniform circular motion, direction of acceleration (centripetal) is always along the centre, which keep changing when particle moves. As, acceleration is vector quantity and its direction is changing, so it can not be constant.

104701.subject: Physics
104701.text: In an interference experiment using two coherent sources of light, the phase difference between the waves arriving at a specific point on the screen is $3\pi$. The fringe formed at this point is a
104701.sol:
For destructive interference (minima), the phase difference must be an odd multiple of $\pi$, given by the condition $\Delta\phi = (2n-1)\pi$, where $n = 1, 2, 3, \dots$ represents the order of the minimum.

Given the phase difference $\Delta\phi = 3\pi$, we can equate:
$(2n-1)\pi = 3\pi$
$2n - 1 = 3$
$2n = 4 \implies n = 2$

Therefore, the fringe formed at this point is the second minimum.

Answer: Second minimum

106997.subject: Chemistry
106997.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
106997.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Antimony(V) oxide ($Sb_2O_5$) is a stronger oxidizing agent than bismuth(V) oxide ($Bi_2O_5$).
Reason (R): The stability of the +5 oxidation state decreases and that of the +3 state increases down Group 15 due to the inert pair effect.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
106997.sol:
Bismuth (Bi) is the heaviest element in Group 15. Due to the strong inert pair effect, the $ns^2$ electrons in Bi are reluctant to participate in bonding, making its +3 oxidation state much more stable than its +5 state.

Because the +5 state of Bi is highly unstable, compounds like $Bi_2O_5$ readily accept electrons to get reduced to the more stable +3 state ($Bi_2O_3$). This makes $Bi_2O_5$ a very strong oxidizing agent, much stronger than $Sb_2O_5$. Therefore, Assertion (A) is false.

The Reason (R) correctly states the general trend for Group 15 elements: the stability of the lower oxidation state (+3) increases and the higher oxidation state (+5) decreases down the group due to the inert pair effect. Thus, Reason (R) is true.

Answer: (A) is false but (R) is true

107029.subject: Chemistry
107029.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
107029.text:
When the first ionization enthalpies ($\Delta_{i}H$) of the second period elements (Li to Ne) are plotted against their atomic numbers ($Z$), the resulting curve exhibits a general upward trend but contains two specific anomalies where the ionization enthalpy drops compared to the preceding element.

Let $P$ represent the element at the first local maximum (peak) and $Q$ represent the element at the local minimum (dip) immediately following it. Similarly, let $R$ represent the element at the second local maximum and $S$ represent the element at the local minimum immediately following it.

Identify the elements $P$, $Q$, $R$, and $S$ respectively.
107029.sol:
In the second period, the first ionization enthalpy generally increases from Li to Ne due to an increase in effective nuclear charge.

However, there are two exceptions (anomalies) that appear as peaks followed by dips on the graph:
1. Beryllium (Be, $2s^{2}$) has a higher ionization enthalpy than Boron (B, $2s^{2} 2p^{1}$) because it is more difficult to remove an electron from a fully filled, more penetrating $2s$ orbital than from a $2p$ orbital. Thus, the first peak $P$ is Be, and the subsequent dip $Q$ is B.
2. Nitrogen (N, $2s^{2} 2p^{3}$) has a higher ionization enthalpy than Oxygen (O, $2s^{2} 2p^{4}$) due to the extra stability of its exactly half-filled $2p$ subshell, which lacks the interelectronic repulsion present in the paired $2p$ orbital of oxygen. Thus, the second peak $R$ is N, and the subsequent dip $S$ is O.

Therefore, $P = \text{Be}$, $Q = \text{B}$, $R = \text{N}$, and $S = \text{O}$.

Answer: $P = \text{Be}$, $Q = \text{B}$, $R = \text{N}$, $S = \text{O}$

108641.subject: Chemistry
108641.text: An ideal gas undergoes isothermal expansion into a vacuum. Which of the following correctly represents the thermodynamic changes for this process?
108641.sol:
Expansion into a vacuum is called free expansion. In a vacuum, the external pressure is zero ($P_{ext} = 0$).

Work done, $w = -P_{ext}\Delta V = 0$.

For an ideal gas undergoing an isothermal process, the change in temperature is zero ($\Delta T = 0$). Since the internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature, the change in internal energy is zero ($\Delta U = 0$).

According to the first law of thermodynamics:
$\Delta U = q + w$
$0 = q + 0 \Rightarrow q = 0$

Therefore, $q = 0$, $w = 0$, and $\Delta U = 0$.

Answer: $q = 0$, $w = 0$, $\Delta U = 0$

Since the process is isothermal, the change in internal energy $\Delta U = 0$. According to the first law of thermodynamics, $q = \Delta U - W = 0$. However, because the volume increases, the entropy of the system increases ($\Delta S_{\text{sys}} = nR \ln(V_2/V_1) > 0$).

Reason (R) is false: Entropy is a state function, not a path function. The change in entropy of the system is independent of the actual irreversible path taken. It is calculated using a hypothetical reversible path between the same initial and final states.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false

108969.subject: Chemistry
108969.text:
At a given temperature, the equilibrium constant for the reaction
$\mathrm{SO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{SO}_3(\mathrm{g})$ is $K_1$.

The equilibrium constant $K_2$ for the reaction
$2\mathrm{SO}_3(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{SO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g})$
is related to $K_1$ as:
108969.sol:
The given initial reaction is:
$\mathrm{SO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{SO}_3(\mathrm{g}) ; K_1$

Reversing this reaction inverses the equilibrium constant:
$\mathrm{SO}_3(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{SO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) ; K' = \dfrac{1}{K_1}$

Multiplying the reversed reaction by a factor of 2 raises the equilibrium constant to the power of 2:
$2\mathrm{SO}_3(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{SO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) ; K_2 = (K')^2$

Substituting the value of $K'$:
$K_2 = \left(\dfrac{1}{K_1}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{K_1^2}$

Answer: $K_2 = \dfrac{1}{K_1^2}$

114351.subject: Chemistry
114351.text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : The mass of a substance altered at an electrode during electrolysis is directly proportional to the quantity of electricity passed.
Statement II : When the same quantity of electricity is passed through solutions of different electrolytes connected in series, the number of moles of the substances deposited is directly proportional to their chemical equivalent weights.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
114351.sol:
Statement I is the exact definition of Faraday's first law of electrolysis, hence it is correct.

Statement II is incorrect. According to Faraday's second law of electrolysis, when the same quantity of electricity is passed through solutions of different electrolytes connected in series, the masses of the substances deposited are directly proportional to their chemical equivalent weights. The number of moles deposited is inversely proportional to the valency ($n$-factor) of the respective ions, not directly proportional to their equivalent weights.

Therefore, Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

Answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

116332.text: Identify the pair of species in which the first species contains exclusively $p\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bonds and the second species contains $d\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bonds.
116332.sol:
Nitrogen belongs to the second period and its valence shell configuration is $2s^2 2p^3$. Since it lacks vacant d-orbitals, it can only form $p\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bonds (e.g., in $\text{N}_2$, $\text{NO}_2^-$, $\text{NO}_3^-$).

Phosphorus and sulphur belong to the third period and have vacant d-orbitals in their valence shells. Thus, they can form $d\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bonds with oxygen (e.g., in $\text{PO}_4^{3-}$, $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$).

In the given options, $\text{NO}_3^-$ contains exclusively $p\pi$-$p\pi$ bonds, while $\text{PO}_4^{3-}$ contains $d\pi$-$p\pi$ bonds. Therefore, the correct pair is $\text{NO}_3^-$ and $\text{PO}_4^{3-}$.

Answer: $\text{NO}_3^-$ and $\text{PO}_4^{3-}$

116898.text:
Which of the following statements are correct?

(B) The higher oxidation states of first row d-block elements get stabilized by oxide ion

(C) Aqueous solution of ${Cr}^{2 +}$ can liberate hydrogen from dilute acid

116898.sol:
The valence electronic configuration of ${Mn}^{3 +}$ is $3{d}^{4}$ and that of ${Mn}^{2 +}$ is stable $3{d}^{5}$.The valence electronic configuration of ${Fe}^{3 +}$ is $3{d}^{5}$ and that of ${Fe}^{2 +}$ is $3{d}^{6}$.

The reduction electrode potential of ${Mn}^{3 +} / {Mn}^{2 +}$ is $+ 1 . 57V$ while that of ${Fe}^{3 +} / {Fe}^{2 +}$ is $+ 0 . 77V$, hence A is wrong. Higher oxidation state of smaller $d$-block elements is stabilised (or say form compounds) with smaller anion oxide that can be explained by stearic reason hence $B$ is correct.

The oxidation electrode potential of ${Cr}^{2 +} / {Cr}^{3 +}$ is $+ 0 . 41V$ hence, it can reduce ${H}^{+}$ and so liberate ${H}_{2}$.

The unpaired electrons in ${V}^{2 +}$ are $3$ hence, the magnetic moment of ${V}^{2 +}$ will be lesser than $4 . 4BM$.

Hence, only $B$ and $C$ are correct.

117117.subject: Chemistry
117117.text: An aqueous divalent ion ($\mathrm{M}^{2+}$) of a $3d$ transition element exhibits a 'spin-only' magnetic moment of $5.92 \text{ BM}$. Which of the following statements correctly describes a property of the neutral element $\mathrm{M}$?
options: The neutral atom possesses an anomalous ground state electronic configuration of $3d^5 4s^1$.
The element exhibits a maximum oxidation state of $+7$ in its compounds.
The element belongs to group 8 of the modern periodic table.
The neutral atom has a completely filled $3d$ subshell.
117117.sol:
The spin-only magnetic moment ($\mu$) is given by $\sqrt{n(n+2)} \text{ BM}$, where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons.

Given $\mu = 5.92 \text{ BM}$, we have $\sqrt{n(n+2)} = 5.92$, which gives $n = 5$.

The divalent ion $\mathrm{M}^{2+}$ belongs to the $3d$ series and has 5 unpaired electrons, so its outer electronic configuration must be $3d^5$.

The neutral atom $\mathrm{M}$ is formed by adding two electrons to the $4s$ orbital, giving the configuration $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^5 4s^2$. This corresponds to Manganese ($\mathrm{Mn}$).

Manganese belongs to group 7 and exhibits a maximum oxidation state of $+7$ (e.g., in $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$).

The configuration $3d^5 4s^1$ belongs to Chromium ($\mathrm{Cr}$). Group 8 corresponds to Iron ($\mathrm{Fe}$).

Answer: The element exhibits a maximum oxidation state of $+7$ in its compounds.

Protic solvents - those that contain $-\mathrm{OH}$ or $-\mathrm{NH}$ group are generally the worst solvents for $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}}$. Polar protic solvents, (like water, alcohols and carboxylic acids), which have strong dipoles but don't have $-\mathrm{OH}$ or $-\mathrm{NH}$ groups are the best. In contrast to protic solvents, which decrease the rates of $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}} 2$ reactants by lowering the ground state energy of nucleophile, polar aprotic solvents (DMF) increase the rates of $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}} 2$ reactions by raising the ground state energy of nucleophile.

123532.subject: Botany
123532.text: How many daughter cells are formed during the cell cycle?
123532.sol: Cell division is a very important process in all living organisms. During the division of a cell, DNA replication and cell growth also take place. All these processes, i.e., cell division, DNA replication, and cell growth, hence, have to take place in a coordinated way to ensure correct division and formation of progeny cells containing intact genomes. The sequence of events by which a cell duplicates its genome, synthesises the other constituents of the cell and eventually divides into two daughter cells is termed cell cycle. Although cell growth (in terms of cytoplasmic increase) is a continuous process, DNA synthesis occurs only during one specific stage in the cell cycle.

Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
125637.sol:
According to the chemiosmotic hypothesis, the primary acceptor of electrons is located towards the outer side of the thylakoid membrane. It transfers its electron not to an electron carrier, but to an H-carrier (plastoquinone). Therefore, Assertion (A) is false.

This H-carrier removes a proton from the stroma while transporting an electron. When it passes the electron to the electron carrier on the inner side of the membrane, the proton is released into the lumen. This mechanism is crucial for developing the proton gradient across the membrane. Therefore, Reason (R) is true.

Answer: (A) is false but (R) is true

A typical angiosperm embryo sac consists of an egg apparatus at the micropylar end, three antipodal cells at the chalazal end, and a large central cell.

127837.sol: Biotic or ecological succession is the formation of a series of biotic communities at the same site over a period of time one after the other, till a stable climax community develops over the area. 128278.subject: Zoology
128278.text: What is the function of pars distalis of pituitary gland?
options: Stores and releases oxytocin and vasopressin
Produces growth hormone (GH), prolactin (PRL), thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH), adrenocorticotrophic hormone (ACTH), luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle stimulating hormone (FSH)
128278.sol: hormone (TSH), adrenocorticotrophic hormone (ACTH), luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) The pituitary gland is located in a bony cavity called sella tursica and is attached to hypothalamus by a stalk (Figure 19.2). It is divided anatomically into an adenohypophysis and a neurohypophysis. Adenohypophysis consists of two portions, pars distalis and pars intermedia. The pars distalis region of pituitary, commonly called anterior pituitary, produces growth hormone (GH), prolactin (PRL), thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH), adrenocorticotrophic hormone (ACTH), luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle stimulating hormone (FSH). Pars intermedia secretes only one hormone called melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH). However, in humans, the pars intermedia is almost merged with pars distalis. Neurohypophysis (pars nervosa) also known as posterior pituitary, stores and releases two hormones called oxytocin and vasopressin, which are actually synthesised by the hypothalamus and are transported axonally to neurohypophysis.

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In frogs, dissolved oxygen in water is exchanged through the skin by simple diffusion.
Reason (R): On land, the buccal cavity, skin, and lungs act as the respiratory organs in frogs.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
130106.sol:
The Assertion (A) is true because in water, frogs rely on cutaneous respiration where dissolved oxygen is exchanged across the highly vascularized moist skin via simple diffusion.

The Reason (R) is also true as adult frogs are amphibious and utilize the buccal cavity, skin, and lungs (pulmonary respiration) for gas exchange when on land.

However, (R) does not explain (A). The mechanism of simple diffusion across the skin is a physical process driven by concentration gradients, which is independent of the anatomical adaptations for terrestrial respiration mentioned in (R).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

130250.subject: Zoology
130250.text: How many pairs of ribs are present in the human body?
130250.sol: .The human body consists of 206 bones in total. These bones are grouped into two main divisions - the axial skeleton and the appendicular skeleton. The skull is composed of two sets of bones, cranial and facial, that total to 22 bones.Each vertebra has a central hollow portion (neural canal) through which the spinal cord passes. The vertebral column is differentiated into cervical (7), thoracic (12), lumbar (5), sacral (1-fused) and coccygeal (1-fused) regions. There are 12 pairs of ribs in the human body.Each rib is connected ventrally to the sternum.The first seven pairs of ribs are called true ribs.The 8th, 9th and 10th pairs of ribs are called vertebrochondral (false) ribs.Joints are essential for all types of movements involving the bony parts of the body. Locomotory movements are no exception to this. Force generated by the muscles is used to carry out movement through joints.Fibrous joints are joints in which bones are held together by fibrous connective tissue. They are usually immovable or slightly movable.

131274.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the cells of gametogenesis and their chromosome numbers in humans.

List-IList-II
A. Primary spermatocyteI. 23 chromosomes
B. Secondary oocyteII. 46 chromosomes
C. Spermatid
D. Oogonia

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
131274.sol:
Primary spermatocytes are diploid cells formed by the differentiation of spermatogonia, thus containing 46 chromosomes.

Secondary oocytes are formed after the completion of Meiosis I (a reductional division), so they are haploid and contain 23 chromosomes.

Spermatids are formed after Meiosis II and are haploid, containing 23 chromosomes.

Oogonia are the diploid mother cells in the ovary, containing 46 chromosomes.

Answer: A-II, B-I, C-I, D-II

132290.subject: Zoology
132290.text: Which syndrome results from an extra copy of chromosome 21?
132290.sol: The chromosomal disorders on the other hand are caused due to absence or excess or abnormal arrangement of one or more chromosomes. Failure of segregation of chromatids during cell division cycle results in the gain or loss of a chromosome(s), called aneuploidy. For example, Down’s syndrome results in the gain of extra copy of chromosome 21. Similarly, Turner’s syndrome results due to loss of an X chromosome in human females. Failure of cytokinesis after telophase stage of cell division results in an increase in a whole set of chromosomes in an organism and, this phenomenon is known as polyploidy. This condition is often seen in plants. The total number of chromosomes in a normal human cell is 46 (23 pairs). Out of these 22 pairs are autosomes and one pair of chromosomes are sex chromosome. Sometimes, though rarely, either an additional copy of a chromosome may be included in an individual or an individual may lack one of any one pair of chromosomes. These situations are known as trisomy or monosomy of a chromosome, respectively. Such a situation leads to very serious consequences in the individual. Down’s syndrome, Turner’s syndrome, Klinefelter’s syndrome are common examples of chromosomal disorders

132700.subject: Zoology
132700.text: During his journey, which island did Darwin visit that sparked his observations on evolution?
132700.sol: During his journey Darwin went to Galapagos Islands. There he observed an amazing diversity of creatures. Of particular interest, small black birds Later Darwin’s Finches amazed him. He realized that there were many varieties of finches on the same island. All the varieties, he conjectured, evolved on the island itself. From the original seed-eating features, many other forms with altered beaks arose, enabling them to become insectivorous and vegetarian finches . This process of evolution of different species in a given geographical area starting from a point and literally radiating to other areas of geography (habitats) is called adaptive radiation. Darwin’s finches represent one of the best examples of this phenomenon. Another example is Australian marsupials. A number of marsupials, each different from the other, evolved from an ancestral stock, but all within the Australian island continent.

133251.subject: Zoology
133251.text: What is the function of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT)?
133251.sol: The primary lymphoid organs in the human body are the bone marrow and thymus, where immature lymphocytes differentiate into antigen-sensitive lymphocytes. There is lymphoid tissue also located within the lining of the major tracts (respiratory, digestive and urogenital tracts) called mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT). It constitutes about 50% of the lymphoid tissue in the human body.The thymus is quite large at the time of birth but keeps reducing in size with age. By the time puberty is attained, it reduces to a very small size. The spleen mainly contains lymphocytes and phagocytes. It acts as a filter of the blood by trapping blood-borne microorganisms. It also has a large reservoir of erythrocytes.
